Retrieval is turned into agent-planned compositional traversal — the agent uses wiki_search and wiki_read, follows bridge links (A→B→answer), or browses directory indices, stopping on traced chains or a tool-call budget [2605.25480#s11.p2][2605.25480#s12.p2][2605.25480#s13.p1]. WiCER's loop is reactive: it evaluates the compiled wiki with one diagnostic probe per source document, and any probe scoring 1/5 triggers diagnosis of the dropped facts, which are fed back as preservation constraints (pinning) in the next compilation — i.e., CEGAR where the document collection is the concrete system, the wiki the abstraction, a score-1 probe the counterexample, and pinning the refinement [2605.07068#s36.p1][2605.07068#s37.p1]. Streaming Knowledge Compilation (Online WiCER) removes the static-corpus assumption and replaces this reactive, probe-driven pinning with proactive pinning driven by a predicted materiality signal φ̂_t, which scores a document's importance for an entity and serves as a query-relevance surrogate, so facts are pinned before any query exposes a gap; it adds decay-weighted eviction and periodic full recompilation every T_r steps, with regret O(√(T log K)) plus a prediction-error term [2606.09877#s2.p3][2606.09877#s31.p2][2606.09877#s43.p3]. The key conceptual shift is in what counts as a counterexample: under 'predictive CEGAR' the counterexample is a predicted high-materiality news item rather than an observed QA failure, moving refinement from diagnosis to prediction [2606.09877#s42.p1][2606.09877#s42.p4]. Queries remain the measurement instrument and consumer but never drive pinning, since they arrive after the news batch [2606.09877#s19.p1][2606.09877#s19.p2].

HippoRAG organizes long-term memory as an LLM-extracted knowledge graph: an instruction-tuned LLM performs OpenIE to extract schemaless KG triples from passages, synonymy edges are added by embedding similarity, and retrieval runs Personalized PageRank over this graph to score passages [2405.14831#s5.p2][2405.14831#s6.p1][2405.14831#s6.p4]. It is inspired by hippocampal indexing, with the KG acting as the hippocampal index [2405.14831#s2.p4][2405.14831#s1.p1].

TrajWiki instead compiles dialogue memory into a persistent wiki layer of pages (index, entity, topic, inventory) that link to provenance-linked trajectories of immutable snapshots, and retrieves hierarchically: query → top wiki pages → linked trajectories → snapshots and source messages [2608.00967#s8.p3][2608.00967#s8.p5][2608.00967#s9.p2][2608.00967#s9.p8]. The wiki organizes memory without replacing source evidence, and answers must be grounded in retrieved source references [2608.00967#s8.p9][2608.00967#s9.p11].

So the key difference: HippoRAG uses a graph of extracted triples as a single associative index for passage retrieval, whereas TrajWiki uses wiki pages as a semantic routing layer over temporally evolving, source-grounded memory trajectories, preserving provenance and claim revision history rather than a flat KG [2608.00967#s7.p8][2608.00967#s9.p1].

respuesta:
HippoRAG organizes retrieved information as a knowledge graph: an LLM extracts schemaless KG triples from each passage via OpenIE, dense encoders add synonymy edges, and the resulting open KG serves as a hippocampal index [2405.14831#s5.p2][2405.14831#s6.p1]. At query time, query entities are linked to KG nodes and Personalized PageRank propagates over the graph, with the node distribution multiplied by a passage-node count matrix to rank passages [2405.14831#s6.p4]. Because the index is a graph, multi-hop reasoning happens in a single retrieval step, and new knowledge is integrated simply by adding edges [2405.14831#s2.p5][2405.14831#s18.p3]. HippoRAG 2 keeps this mapping but adds passage nodes with "contains" edges and an LLM filter over retrieved triples before seeding PPR [2502.14802#s7.p3][2502.14802#s9.p1][2502.14802#s10.p1].

TrajWiki instead compiles memory into a wiki layer of pages p=(η, y, h, L_p) with four types (index, entity, topic, inventory) that link to memory trajectories [2608.00967#s8.p3][2608.00967#s8.p5]. The underlying memory is not a graph of triples but append-only trajectories of immutable episodic snapshots with claim-level ADD/REVISE/DEPRECATE operations, where revised or deprecated claims are never deleted [2608.00967#s7.p1][2608.00967#s7.p8][2608.00967#s7.p9]. Retrieval is hierarchical and fixed rather than graph propagation: a query is routed to top-t wiki pages, their links induce a candidate trajectory set, and trajectories are selected and expanded into evidence tuples with source references [2608.00967#s9.p2][2608.00967#s9.p5][2608.00967#s9.p8]. The wiki organizes memory without replacing source evidence, and wiki summaries alone reach gold trajectory recall 0.807 but zero gold source-reference coverage [2608.00967#s8.p9][2608.00967#s36.p4].

In short, HippoRAG's organizing structure is an entity/triple knowledge graph traversed by PPR for one-step multi-hop retrieval, while TrajWiki's is a human-readable wiki of pages that routes to provenance-linked trajectory snapshots, preserving how beliefs evolved rather than only associations between entities [2405.14831#s2.p5][2608.00967#s2.p2][2608.00967#s9.p2].

HippoRAG organizes long-term memory as an LLM-extracted knowledge graph used as a hippocampal index: OpenIE triples plus synonymy edges form a schemaless KG, and retrieval runs Personalized PageRank over that graph from query-linked nodes to score passages [2405.14831#s5.p2][2405.14831#s6.p1][2405.14831#s6.p4]. TrajWiki instead compiles memory into a persistent wiki of human-readable pages (`index`, `entity`, `topic`, `inventory`), each linking a set of source-grounded trajectories, and retrieves hierarchically: query → top-t pages → linked trajectories → snapshots/source messages [2608.00967#s8.p3][2608.00967#s8.p5][2608.00967#s9.p2][2608.00967#s9.p8]. So HippoRAG's index is a graph of entities/triples traversed by PPR, while TrajWiki's is a page-level semantic directory whose links route to provenance-linked evidence; wiki routing is a lossy filter that cuts the candidate universe from 130.4 to 55.6 while coverage falls from 0.610 to 0.356 [2608.00967#s15.p1], and wiki summaries alone give zero gold source-reference coverage, so pages cannot replace source evidence [2608.00967#s36.p4].

HippoRAG associates information across passages at index/retrieval time: an LLM extracts schemaless OpenIE triples from each passage into a knowledge graph, synonymy edges link similar noun phrases, and retrieval runs Personalized PageRank over this graph so that passages sharing entities/concepts are connected even when the relevant entities never co-occur in one passage [2405.14831#s2.p3][2405.14831#s5.p2][2405.14831#s6.p4]. It is a graph-based associative index (a hippocampal index) for multi-hop retrieval, not a conflict-resolution mechanism.

TOKI instead addresses contradictions in persistent agent memory as write-time concurrency control: a bitemporal fact (valid time, system time, provenance, confidence) is compared against existing facts, and two facts contradict when they share subject and predicate but disagree on object with overlapping valid-time periods [2606.06240#s6.p1]. Contradictions are resolved by typed bitemporal operators (last-writer-wins, evidence-weighted merge, await-confirmation, per-rule policy), each with an isolation precondition and admitted anomalies, returning a winner, invalidating the loser in system time, and emitting an audit tuple [2606.06240#s10.p1][2606.06240#s2.p5]. It also guards against LLM-specific anomalies (replay inconsistency, belief-drift skew, audit erasure) via a keyed judge log [2606.06240#s11.p1][2606.06240#s15.p2].

So the difference: HippoRAG links passages associatively through a shared graph index and PPR-based propagation at retrieval, with no notion of contradiction or overwriting; TOKI resolves conflicting facts at write time through bitemporal operators with isolation levels, audit rows, and judge logs, with no graph-based cross-passage association.

respuesta: The two papers treat contradiction resolution and persistence semantics very differently. The Missing Knowledge Layer paper makes persistence semantics the organizing principle: each cognitive layer gets its own persistence mechanism, and for the Knowledge layer ("what is true") persistence is indefinite with supersession — old claims are preserved and linked to successors with provenance rather than forgotten [2604.11364#s8.p1][2604.11364#s7.p3]. Contradiction resolution is thus a property of the Knowledge layer's supersession semantics, distinct from Memory's Ebbinghaus decay and bi-temporal event sourcing [2604.11364#s9.p1]; the paper notes BEAM shows all systems scoring worst on contradiction resolution (<0.05) at 10M tokens, an ability it argues needs architectural rather than retrieval solutions [2604.11364#s13.p6], and its pilot improved contradiction resolution from 0.394 to 0.500 with typed routing [2604.11364#s20.p9]. respuesta:

Missing Knowledge Layer paper: it argues each cognitive layer needs its own persistence mechanism, and that conflating them is a category error — systems apply decay to facts or give facts and experiences identical update mechanics [2604.11364#s1.p1]. Knowledge persists indefinitely and is updated by supersession: old claims are preserved and linked to successors with provenance, i.e. contradicted facts are superseded, not forgotten [2604.11364#s8.p1]. Memory instead decays (Ebbinghaus) and uses bi-temporal event sourcing [2604.11364#s9.p1]. The organizing litmus is storage-level vs query-time: recency is a query-time heuristic, decay a storage-level mechanism [2604.11364#s12.p1]. Contradiction resolution is thus a storage-level property; BEAM's near-zero contradiction resolution (<0.05) is attributed to missing storage-level mechanisms rather than retrieval quality [2604.11364#s13.p6], and typed routing to supersession-aware/bi-temporal stores raised contradiction resolution from 0.394 to 0.500 [2604.11364#s20.p9].

Each operator returns a winner with a system-time invalidation of the loser and emits an audit tuple [2606.06240#s10.p1]. Persistence is made explicit via the dual-row schema (current vs. audit rows) so the overwritten fact is retained [2606.06240#s9.p1], and audit erasure (N3) is a schema-level anomaly defended by the audit row [2606.06240#s11.p1]. The audit row dominates the loser's provenance under the semiring natural order, so audit erasure cannot occur [2606.06240#s13.p3].

In short, both characterize contradiction resolution as a write-time/storage-level persistence decision whose semantics must preserve superseded facts with provenance, rather than as a query-time filter or a decay/delete operation [2604.11364#s8.p1][2606.06240#s10.p1].

They differ in whether conflicting/stale information is actively removed. HippoRAG (and HippoRAG 2) is an indexing/retrieval framework: it builds an LLM-extracted knowledge graph (OpenIE triples plus synonym and passage nodes) and retrieves via Personalized PageRank [2405.14831#s5.p2][2502.14802#s7.p4][2502.14802#s8.p2]. It has no mechanism for handling new or conflicting information—new passages are simply added to the graph, and nothing excises superseded states; the pages describe no update/conflict-resolution procedure [2405.14831#s6.p4][2502.14802#s11.p1]. GC-Mem, by contrast, is an inference-time consistency protocol aimed exactly at this: it formalizes Semantic Shadowing, where an updated entity's old state is not deleted and dense retrieval returns the majority of stale contradictory chunks [2609.16073#s2.p2]. GC-Mem applies a temporal dominance operator Φ_T with a pairwise NLI contradiction detector over the retrieved candidate set, excising any older chunk contradicted by a newer one, so that if a valid chunk is retrieved P(y=S_new)→1 [2609.16073#s9.p4][2609.16073#s9.p5]. It is bounded by detector recall (>50% needed) and adds O(k²) cost [2609.16073#s20.p1][2609.16073#s20.p2]. In short: HippoRAG accumulates and associates without conflict handling, while GC-Mem prunes temporally dominated conflicting memories at query time [2609.16073#s1.p1].

They differ in where and how conflicts are resolved. HippoRAG (and HippoRAG 2) is a retrieval framework with no explicit conflict-resolution or update mechanism: it builds an offline knowledge graph from OpenIE triples plus synonym edges and passage nodes [2405.14831#s5.p2][2502.14802#s7.p4][2502.14802#s8.p2], and at query time links the query to triples, filters them with an LLM, and runs Personalized PageRank to rank passages [2502.14802#s9.p1][2502.14802#s10.p1][2502.14802#s11.p1]. New information is simply indexed into the graph; nothing detects or removes contradictory older content, so on FactConsolidation (overwriting outdated facts with newer contradictory ones) HippoRAG-v2 reaches only 54.0 single-hop and 5.0 multi-hop [2507.05257#s21.p3]. GC-Mem instead targets exactly this case: it keeps the store append-only but, at inference time, applies a temporal dominance operator Φ_T that uses a pairwise NLI contradiction oracle within the retrieved candidate set to excise any chunk contradicted by a newer one [2609.16073#s9.p2][2609.16073#s9.p4], so chained mutations collapse to the terminal state [2609.16073#s5.p2]. This lifts conflict-resolution accuracy to 97.3% on deepseek-v3 Large versus 56.8% for standard RAG [2609.16073#s14.p3], though it depends on detector recall above 50% [2609.16073#s20.p1]. In short: HippoRAG integrates new passages into a graph index without adjudicating conflicts, whereas GC-Mem leaves storage untouched and prunes contradicted older chunks per query via recency-based contradiction detection [2609.16073#s1.p1].
